answer: A farmer's cheapest trick is copying one good worker 10,000 times and flooding the market like a gale. Stop it by requiring every identity to submit a distinct trained model each epoch, scored on a hidden test set. An independent evaluator compares output vectors: any group above 0.95 similarity falls into the same canyon and is quarantined as one operator, its rewards withheld. Passing honestly costs $25 in compute and 2 hours of curation per model, so 10,000 fakes cost $250,000 plus 20,000 hours. Like an opal, a real model refracts test data its own way; copies shine identically.
